clue.text: Take as relevant

definitions.meaning: to take something for your own use, as a verb
suitable or fitting for the occasion, as an adjective

explanation.surface: Someone is told to regard a remark as pertinent.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means seize for oneself and the adjective means suitable; one spelling covers both senses, said differently.

clue.text: Handled receptacle giving small page trouble

parts.note: P is the usual short form of page
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A bucket handle causes a young page some bother.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucket is a container with a hoop-shaped handle for carrying.

clue.text: Laughing about the continental being so trusting

indicators.note: about here means going round, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: riant is a literary word for laughing or cheerful
el is the Spanish word for the, a continental article

explanation.surface: A cheerful European is described as naive and full of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal here, not 're'; the laughing word is a rare English borrowing from French meaning smiling.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who depends on others with confidence is trusting in them.

clue.text: Quietly made a meal of savoury food

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to make a meal is to eat, so ate

explanation.surface: Someone silently scoffed a tasty dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Pâté is a rich paste of meat or fish spread on toast.

clue.text: Lofty hotheads? Far from it!

parts.note: high frozen coverings on mountain tops or poles are the opposite of hot heads: cold tops high up

explanation.surface: An exclamation dismissing arrogant, quick-tempered people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hotheads' suggests angry people; the clue asks for heads that are lofty but freezing rather than hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar and mountain sheets of permanent frozen water sit on top of the world like cold coverings.

clue.text: To one over fifty this will be hard work

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: A remark that hard graft awaits anyone past fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Toil is a synonym of labour, strenuous effort.

clue.text: Their business is increasing naturally

parts.note: describes people or heated boxes whose job is to grow and multiply plants by natural means

explanation.surface: A firm whose trade is growing organically.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a company report on organic growth; the clue means breeding plants or animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners and seed trays that raise new plants from seeds or cuttings multiply stock by nature.

clue.text: Outlaw hit and killed by mistake

indicators.note: by mistake suggests the letters landed in the wrong order and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bandit struck someone and accidentally killed them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistake' signals the anagram of HIT and KILLED BY; 'by' is part of the fodder as well as reading naturally with 'mistake'.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Wild West gunslinger was a fugitive from the law.

clue.text: Check imposed on correspondence, and that's capital!

indicators.note: in a down clue imposed on means placed on top of the next piece

parts.note: to check something is to block it
a letter is a piece of correspondence

explanation.surface: Censorship of mail delights someone who exclaims it is splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like an exclamation of approval; it is a capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain upper-case characters, as on forms, are capitals.

clue.text: Huns — dreaded maybe, though really quite stupid people

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Feared invaders turn out to be dim-witted in reality.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunces or blockheads are very slow-witted folk.

clue.text: A little crawler with sterling qualities?

definitions.text: A little crawler with sterling qualities?

parts.words: A little crawler with sterling qualities?
parts.note: a tiny eight-legged creature said in folklore to bring wealth, with sterling meaning British cash

explanation.surface: A small sycophant of excellent character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crawler' suggests a toady and 'sterling' fine character; it is a tiny spider thought to bring luck with cash. Sterling is the British pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny British spider that superstition says brings riches if it runs over you.

clue.text: Spin a record

definitions.meaning: a list or register of names

explanation.surface: Playing a vinyl disc on a turntable.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn over and over, and a register such as an electoral list.

clue.text: Game though loud eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, telling us to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: A board game that is noisy yet quirky.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's board game played with dice and counters.

clue.text: Preparing for a getaway

parts.note: reads as a criminal planning an escape but means filling suitcases before a holiday

explanation.surface: A gang readies itself to flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getaway' suggests a criminal escape; it is a holiday break.
explanation.definitionFit: Filling suitcases is what holidaymakers do before going away.

clue.text: This man, being German, trains

parts.note: RY, railway, stands for trains

explanation.surface: A German fellow undergoes training.
explanation.walkthrough: Gerry is a man's name and also old slang for a German, so the surface fits the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name, so a particular fellow.

clue.text: See about a mere foot

indicators.note: about here means going round, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: taken as written
a mere is a lake or pond

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at a measurement of only twelve inches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. 'foot' is a metrical foot in verse, not a measure of length.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody a metrical unit of two stressed syllables is one such foot.

clue.text: Mails mis-sorted, causing a stew

indicators.note: post that is mis-sorted is put into the wrong order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Badly sorted post gets a postal worker into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a stew' looks like a state of agitation; it is a ragout of game birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich ragout of game birds is a kind of stew.

clue.text: Drink's taken around ten in America

indicators.note: around tells us one piece goes round the other

parts.note: teas are drinks; the 's supplies the plural S
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A tea is taken round ten o'clock somewhere in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lone Star State is a place in the United States.

clue.text: Note antique and very valuable stuff

parts.note: G is a musical note
antique means old

explanation.surface: A banknote that is ancient is worth a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow precious metal is a valuable material.

clue.text: A girl pupil's environs

definitions.meaning: the coloured ring around the pupil of the eye

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl's surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' suggests a schoolchild but is the dark centre of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, and the coloured membrane encircling the dark centre of the eye.

clue.text: A European city giving its name to a perfume

parts.note: Roma is the Italian name of Rome

explanation.surface: A fragrance named after a continental city.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant smell or scent.

clue.text: Artist set up secure high-level lighting

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is an artist
to clamp is to secure

explanation.surface: A painter fixes bright lights overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: An intensely bright electric lamp is used for powerful overhead illumination.

clue.text: A person writing to arrange credit

parts.note: a scribe is someone who writes

explanation.surface: A writer is hired to organise a loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to arrange' is a loose link; 'credit' is the verb, to attribute.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit someone with something is to attribute it to them.

clue.text: Staggering — like the salvage collectors?

definitions.meaning: totters are rag-and-bone men, British scrap collectors, so this is a playful adjective from them

explanation.surface: Reeling, like old rag-and-bone men.
explanation.walkthrough: A totter is British slang for a rag-and-bone man who collects scrap from door to door.
explanation.definitionFit: Wobbly or unsteady, and humorously resembling scrap-collecting totters.

clue.text: Foreigner given a rise, possibly one pound

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, from libra
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A foreign worker gets a pay rise of perhaps a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of a Middle Eastern state is a foreigner to a British solver.

clue.text: Fishing equipment set right, fish

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Angling kit is put in order and a fish caught.
explanation.definitionFit: The winding spool on an angler's rod holds the line.

clue.text: Preceded a wife of the king of Sparta

definitions.text: wife of the king of Sparta

parts.note: to lead is to go before, so preceded means led

explanation.surface: Someone went ahead of a Spartan queen.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the mother of Helen was married to Tyndareus, a Spartan ruler.

clue.text: Had in view new cut

parts.note: to have in view is to see, so had in view is saw

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a fresh slice.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber that has been sliced through with a toothed blade.

clue.text: Some will become avid letter-writers when unemployed

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: Jobless people take to writing letters keenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without work is out of a job, at a loose end.

clue.text: To do with Erin's constitution

indicators.note: constitution means how something is made up, so the letters are built anew

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Concerning the Irish constitution.
explanation.walkthrough: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland; 'constitution' rearranges ERIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means concerning or regarding.

clue.text: Irate parson making amends

indicators.note: making here means forming the letters into something new

explanation.surface: An angry clergyman makes up for a wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Compensation paid for a wrong done is a way of making good.

clue.text: A swimmer dived in and performed certain crafty manoeuvres

parts.note: a carp is a fish, a swimmer
to dive in is to enter

explanation.surface: A fish plunged in and did some clever tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crafty' suggests cunning; it means woodworking craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing woodwork is a craft, so this is working at joinery.
